summary: Keep calculated transition energies and strengths tied to method output while showing that an excited state may mix several orbital pairs.
objective: Build an excited-state inspector where I select a calculated spectral line, inspect all printed orbital-pair contributions, and compare signed orbital isosurfaces without treating them as electron trajectories or a complete spectrum.
intent_signals: mixed excited state is not one electron jump
example_prompts: Show calculated ORCA excited states with energy, wavelength and oscillator strength, then inspect a state made from several printed orbital transitions.
negative_signals: Not an experimental spectrum, peak assignment proof, electron movie, total density, complete configuration expansion or accuracy guarantee.
not_for: No broadening/solvent/vibronic spectrum unless supplied, no hidden contributions treated as zero, no orbital population movie, method benchmarking or universal assignment.

entities.name: Transition spectrum rail
entities.guidance: Blender supplies a calibrated rail and reusable state markers. Three.js places lines from supplied values and shows method, geometry, units, root convergence and print threshold.

entities.name: Orbital contribution stage
entities.guidance: Blender may provide neutral molecular staging; Three.js loads provenance-bound signed grids for selected orbitals, uses paired phase surfaces at the same |isovalue| and displays every supplied contribution weight rather than choosing one arrow.

state_contract.model: A finite imported result bundle identifies software/version, method, basis/reference, molecular geometry hash, state/root index, convergence status, excitation energy with unit, optional wavelength, oscillator strength convention and a list of printed orbital-pair contributions with coefficients/weights and print threshold. Orbital grids separately identify orbital index/spin, geometry hash, scalar quantity/unit, grid dimensions, origin, three grid-axis step vectors/basis, data ordering and paired ±isovalue of equal magnitude. Reject mismatched geometry/method/root or nonfinite values. A state with several supplied contributions remains a mixture; omitted-below-threshold weight is unknown, not zero. Optional sticks use supplied transition energies/strengths only; broadening is disabled unless a sourced kernel/width is explicitly provided.
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns result parsing, provenance matching, line/contribution selection and signed surfaces. Blender owns only illustrative stage assets; an external quantum-chemistry calculation owns numerical output.
actions: Select a converged state and inspect energy, wavelength, oscillator strength convention and all supplied contributions.
Toggle the supplied canonical orbital-pair grids while retaining coefficients, scalar quantity, grid frame/basis and signed phase legend.
Compare a nearly single-contribution example with a mixed state without animating an electron path.
Reject unconverged roots, geometry-hash mismatch, missing units/threshold or density grids mislabeled as orbitals; reset clears selections.

invariants: Every displayed scalar and orbital grid retains software/method/geometry/root provenance and declared units.
Multiple printed contributions remain visible; a print threshold means the displayed list need not sum to one.
Positive and negative orbital isosurfaces represent sign of a supplied orbital amplitude grid. Their squared amplitude is not total many-electron density.
Calculated stick positions/strengths are method outputs, not a complete experimental spectrum; motion between orbitals is illustrative only.
motion_guidance: Step commits one source frame or declared transformation; pause preserves committed state and reset restores data, view, selections and errors.
Offer a static frame/table alternative. Tweened atom, curve or surface motion explains correspondence only and never creates scientific samples.
creative_affordances: Blender may establish a distinctive molecular stage, lattice frame and stable atom/orbital glyph families; Three.js binds them to scientific IDs and data.
Materials, camera and composition remain flexible when units, provenance, sign, identity and uncertainty stay legible without color alone.
known_limits: One supplied calculation bundle and its printed thresholded contributions. It omits experimental conditions and broadening unless explicitly supplied and makes no accuracy or assignment guarantee.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no chemistry calculation, trajectory conversion, Blender export, browser, renderer or interactive artifact was run.

physical_contract.scope: Scientific coordinates and annotations drive display; mesh contact and animation do not compute chemistry.

object_craft.structure: Build a precise stick-spectrum rail beside a fixed molecule cradle; use paired isosurface shells and a weighted contribution rack instead of a single transfer arrow.
object_craft.material: Use sign-paired surfaces with equal opacity and explicit +/- labels; line strength also has a numeric value and accessible height/pattern cue.

claims.statement: The ORCA 6.1.1 manual shows excited-state output with energies and thresholded individual excitation weights, including states with multiple orbital-pair contributions, and an absorption table containing transition energy, wavelength and oscillator strength.
claims.scope: Documented ORCA output fields and examples; no accuracy, experimental-spectrum completeness or one-electron-path claim.
